description: Technical University of Munich and Fraunhofer IOSB publish TUM-MLS-2018, a mobile laser-scanning benchmark of the TUM City Campus in Munich, Germany. Provider documentation dates acquisition to 19 December 2018 using two Velodyne HDL-64E scanners on a vehicle. The test area covers approximately 29,000 square metres around the campus entrance and neighbouring streets. The collection contains more than two billion points in 21,170 PCD files over 17 minutes. Labelled portions distinguish artificial and natural terrain, vegetation, buildings, hardscape, artefacts and vehicles. Sensor positions accompany measured three-dimensional coordinates. This geometry is listed in TUM2TWIN as an input to the campus digital twin. A small sample is publicly linked, while full access is obtained by contacting the named provider teams. The original MLS collection is made available under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Cost is not specified. Caveats include partial manual labels and the need to reconcile reference systems and registration before combining observations from different years. The 2018 documentation explicitly warns that finer registration may be necessary for change detection. The separate 2016 collection is a related time slice. No PCD files, sample archives or FTP bodies were retrieved.
